attacker_capabilities: repeatedly grow a collection before victim action
expected_observation: resource use rises as storage grows, even without changing contract logic.

experiment_plan.attacker_action: Grow the attacker-controlled data set or trigger repeated input processing before a victim call.
experiment_plan.expected_observation: Storage growth creates a resource-exhaustion path should produce progressively higher cost as attacker-controlled state expands.
experiment_plan.falsification_condition: If the victim operation remains flat or bounded despite growth in the attacker-controlled state, the hypothesis is weakened or falsified.
experiment_plan.measurement: Record gas usage and execution cost as the attacker-controlled input size increases.
experiment_plan.setup: Deploy the local contract and initialize attacker-controlled state with a small baseline.
experiment_plan.state_changes: Observe whether attacker-controlled growth causes a larger resource requirement in the victim path.
experiment_plan.victim_action: Call the relevant mutating path in addParticipant, processAll.

mechanism: The contract stores attacker-controlled data and later reprocesses it, creating a path where storage growth increases per-user cost without a bounded limit.
predicted_failure: The contract eventually becomes unusable due to rising persistent storage and processing cost.
target_invariant: Critical state transitions should remain reachable and not become prohibitively expensive.
title: Storage growth creates a resource-exhaustion path
